title: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) in Profile Update - Cross-User Profile Modification
description:
The /profile endpoint is vulnerable to Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR). An authenticated user can read and modify other users' profile data by specifying the target user_id as a query parameter. The application does not properly validate that the authenticated user owns the profile being accessed or modified. This allows any logged-in user to read and modify any other user's profile information including name, lastname, email, loan_amount, loan_term_months, and monthly_payment fields.

The vulnerability exists in both GET requests (information disclosure) and POST requests (unauthorized modification). There is no server-side authorization check to verify resource ownership before allowing access or modifications.
impact:
An attacker can perform complete authorization bypass and unauthorized actions on behalf of other users including:
- Reading sensitive personal information (name, email, loan details)
- Modifying other users' profile data
- Manipulating loan amounts and payment terms
- Altering financial calculations that may depend on these values
- Lateral movement between user accounts
- Impersonation of other users by modifying their profile information
This vulnerability completely undermines the multi-user security model of the application, allowing unauthorized access and modification of all user data.
evidence:
POC execution successfully confirmed the vulnerability:

1. Authenticated as user 1 (test:test)
2. Successfully accessed user 2's profile via: GET /profile?user_id=2
   - Retrieved: Name: NoRef, Email: noref@test.com
3. Successfully modified user 2's profile via: POST /profile?user_id=2
   - Sent modification: name=IDOR_MODIFIED_1764692591, email=attacked_1764692591@test.com, loan_amount=7777
   - Server returned HTTP 302 (redirect - typical success response)
4. Verified modification persisted:
   - Retrieved user 2's profile again
   - Confirmed changes: Name changed to IDOR_MODIFIED_1764692591, Email changed to attacked_1764692591@test.com, Loan amount changed to 7777.0

The vulnerability allows complete read and write access to any user's profile data by manipulating the user_id query parameter.
remediation:
1. Implement proper authorization checks: Verify that the authenticated user owns the profile being accessed/modified before returning or modifying data
2. Remove user_id parameter from client-controllable locations (query string, form data) - use the authenticated session to determine the current user
3. Add server-side validation: Check if user.id from session matches the user_id being accessed. Return HTTP 403 Forbidden if mismatch
4. Pass user_id only through secure session tokens or JWTs, never in client-controllable parameters
5. Implement access control middleware that enforces resource ownership checks on all user-specific endpoints
6. Create a whitelist of endpoints that can accept user_id parameters and ensure proper authorization on each
7. Add comprehensive audit logging for profile access and modifications to detect unauthorized access
8. Test authorization on all user-specific endpoints (/profile, /loan_details, and any others that access user data)
9. Implement role-based access control (RBAC) if needed for admin access to user data
10. Use security testing in CI/CD to prevent regression of authorization bypasses
references: OWASP A01:2021 - Broken Access Control, CWE-639 Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key, CWE-284 Improper Access Control, CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N (CRITICAL - 8.1)
toolCallDescription: Documenting confirmed IDOR vulnerability in /profile endpoint with working POC that demonstrates cross-user profile modification
